request.goal: Minimize the full training step_ms of the original FP32 GPT-2 Medium FSDP2 workload, preserving the source's full two-rank global batch, logits, gradient and two-update parameter quality, numerical policy, completion boundaries and peak_allocated_bytes <=1.05 baseline constraint. notes: Command provenance: user command 'torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 train.py --output /tmp/fsdp-source --profile' (intent.json), matching README.md:3. --output is a required harness artifact directory (framework supplies its own path, not /tmp/fsdp-source as a semantic value); --profile enables the 3 diagnostic communication profile invocations.

The workload object is the complete workload.json row copied verbatim with the project's exact field names (model, world_size, batch_per_rank, sequence_length, seed, learning_rate, warmup, repeats, profile_repeats, quality, objective); it is not wrapped in a new envelope.

Quality semantics are source-required (train.py verify(), 97-137; README.md:10-16): an independent unsharded serial global-batch reference runs quality.continuous_updates=2 complete updates; each reference update accumulates every rank's forward with (loss/world_size).backward(); per step, the actual run's loss, complete logits, every parameter gradient and every post-update parameter must match the reference at atol 1e-6 / rtol 1e-4 (torch.allclose plus finiteness, train.py compare()). Gradients and parameters are compared in their actual DTensor shard layout per rank (reference_shard, train.py:80-86): FSDP shards are different parts of one parameter, not replicas equal across ranks. Discrete exact checks: logits+1 must FAIL the comparison (negative control, train.py:125) and transformer.wte.weight is lm_head.weight must remain true (tied embeddings, train.py:127); the source run fails hard if any check fails (train.py:166-167).

Numerical policy is a semantic requirement (goal statement; README.md:4-6; train.py policy() 20-26 and build_model 29-33): FP32 everywhere, TF32 off for cuda.matmul and cudnn, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), cudnn.benchmark False, eager attention, dropout 0, use_cache False. No generation is involved (use_cache False, labels=input_ids LM loss).

Baseline implementation choices, not frozen requirements (README.md:18-21): the bottom-up per-transformer-block fully_shard FSDP2 strategy, default prefetch scheduling, no manual serialization/barriers, the optimizer implementation and foreach=False grouping, and CPU thread settings (torch.set_num_threads(4), set_num_interop_threads(1)). Semantics-equivalent alternatives are allowed provided the entire work, the quality tolerances above and the peak_allocated_bytes <= 1.05x baseline budget are preserved.

Measurement definition (train.py measured(), 140-148): reset() of all parameters to initial values and zero_grad happen outside timing, then dist.barrier(), torch.cuda.synchronize(), torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(), and wall-clock time.perf_counter_ns around step() closed by a trailing torch.cuda.synchronize(); peak_allocated_bytes and allocated_bytes are sampled while the step's returned loss/logits are still referenced. Aggregation (train.py:169-171): max across ranks per aligned invocation index, then median across the repeats, i.e. ranks_then_samples, matching README.md:23-24. warmup=2 and repeats=5 are the harness's statistical repetitions, outside the per-invocation work.

Communication diagnostics (requested by the goal) are separate profiled invocations, not part of clean timing: workload.json profile_repeats=3; train.py:173-179 does reset, barrier, synchronize, then a torch.profiler CPU+CUDA trace around one step() labeled 'source.complete_training_step' and exports a chrome trace. Sampled via the installed torch_communication collector (deployment.json metric_collectors); communication_kernel_sum_ms includes waiting and is neither wire time nor an exposed critical-path bound (README.md:28-30). Collector availability must be verified by the actual workload worker; failed collection is an error, never a fabricated zero. Profile invocations are rank-aligned (barrier+synchronize), justifying ranks_then_samples aggregation.
--api-fixture (train.py:158-159) shrinks the model to a 2-layer/128-hidden developer API check; it is not this task and does not affect acceptance (README.md:31-32).

trials.rationale: State: the previous joint candidate (trial-4f5fce6e6b, keep_unsharded_tail_k3) was ACCEPTED (quality pass, peak_allocated_bytes exactly at the 2239245312 B baseline, objective 171.46 ms vs parent 175.46 ms; best parameter trial keep=3 measured 170.94 ms) and is installed in the current revision 799a80d2..., so the current accepted timing is ~171 ms, not the 176.15 ms original baseline. Previous feedback contains no failure to repair; this selection is the next continuation step at the same proven editable boundary (model forward b08a96298d855d7c8dcd7497 + the 24 FSDP block modules + the block _allgather_base_ functional family), composing with the installed keep-3 policy rather than replacing it. Measured facts (current-revision nsys, observations/current/nsys-9ed9145c.json, rank 0): the forward all-gather chain (root 105029632 B gather 8.25 ms + 24 block 25192448 B gathers, ~2.0-2.4 ms each, RING over SHM per the NCCL tuning log at these payload sizes) spans 79.43 ms of which only 57.37 ms is NCCL-busy: 22.06 ms of NCCL-idle exposure sits between successive forward all-gathers (24 gaps of 0.42-0.92 ms plus 1.80 ms after the root gather plus one anomalous 5.0 ms stall), and the gap intervals contain the block compute kernels (25 kernels, ~0.3 ms GPU busy per block, plus dispatch latency). In backward the AG/RS chain is already gap-free (~2.1 ms per collective back-to-back, compute hidden), so backward is wire-volume-bound and only volume cuts (memory-gated) can help it. Code-level mechanism verified in the measured worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129: FSDPParamGroup.pre_forward() calls unshard() then wait_for_unshard() synchronously and FSDPState._states_to_forward_prefetch is empty by default, so by default the next block's all-gather is issued only at that block's pre-forward - block compute cannot overlap the next all-gather; the default 'implicit prefetch' only overlaps the next copy-in with the current all-gather. The public FSDPModule.set_modules_to_forward_prefetch([next_block]) API exists precisely to issue the next all-gather at the current block's entry (singleton list = same overlap target, issued earlier from the CPU; depth>=2 needs >=2 unsharded units in flight). This matches the accepted candidate's established pattern: build-time public-API policy mutation on the block modules with route recording through the model-boundary forward and a symmetric build-time agreement all_reduce with rollback to parent delegation. Why this over alternatives: (1) extending keep_unsharded_blocks beyond 3 only removes ~1.95 ms per block (measured slope) and stacks +50.4 MB per block against the 111.96 MB measured headroom; (2) eliminating the root gather/scatter pair (16.5 ms combined spans) via a sharded-wte/lm_head rewrite is a much larger, riskier restructure whose benefit depends on whether module-hook-driven FSDP all-gathers can be bypassed at all under the legacy binding backend - an unverified assumption; (3) the 4090 fabric is SHM with P2P disabled and every observed large collective already runs at ~25 GB/s per rank, so throughput is saturated and overlap is the only remaining lever on existing volume. Memory cost of depth-1 forward prefetch is one extra unsharded block unit (~50.4 MB transient, mid-forward, where the current run holds one unit; the keep-3 tail-retention window is unchanged), i.e. well inside the 1.05x peak budget given the measured keep=3 peak of exactly 2239245312 B; a depth>=2 variant (+~101 MB) is left to the parameter search under the same constraint. Numerics are untouched: identical collectives, payloads, kernel sequence and counts (45 block all-gathers + root, 25 reduce-scatters), only their CPU issue order changes, so logits, gradients, parameters, DTensor shard layouts, completion boundaries and the retained quality-pass scalar are all preserved.
